bug_description.normalized: Importing the staged 444-byte DER `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` through `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8` reaches `pkcs8_key_decrypt`, which reads the outer `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm`, classifies it as `PBES2_GENERIC`, and passes the `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` subspan into `_gnutls_read_pkcs_schema_params`' PBES2 branch. `read_pbkdf2_params` then allocates `char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE]` without initialization and asks `asn1_read_value` for the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm`. In the staged build, `_work/src/build.sh` installs external `/src/libtasn1` into `$DEPS_PATH` before configuring GnuTLS, so the executed decoder is `../libtasn1/lib/decoding.c` plus `../libtasn1/lib/element.c`: the witness OID bytes `06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff` become the short text `0.32.32.32.2097056`, and only `strlen(...)+1 = 19` bytes are copied into `oid`. Line 668 then compares `oid` against the 22-byte `PBKDF2_OID` literal with `strcmp`, and MemorySanitizer reports a use-of-uninitialized-value originating from `oid`'s stack allocation.

source.description: First project-code consumption on the vulnerable path: the raw witness buffer pointer and length are aliased into local datum `_data`, which is then parsed as encrypted PKCS#8.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is a 444-byte DER blob. The harness passes it as `raw.data/raw.size` into `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8(key, &raw, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, "password", 0)`, and lines 1510-1511 alias those exact bytes into `_data` for the later PKCS#8 and PBES2 decoders.

root_cause.description: The stack buffer `oid` is created uninitialized, but later logic treats it as a fully initialized C string after `asn1_read_value` fills only a short prefix.
root_cause.note: The staged build installs external `/src/libtasn1` into `$DEPS_PATH` before configuring GnuTLS (`_work/src/build.sh`:23-26,45), so `asn1_read_value` uses `../libtasn1/lib/decoding.c` and `../libtasn1/lib/element.c`, not the bundled minitasn1 fallback. That path can materialize a short textual OID and copy only `strlen(...)+1` bytes into `oid`; because `oid` is never pre-zeroed and line 668 ignores the returned `len`, bytes after the copied NUL remain indeterminate. The staged `patch.diff` and `fixed_commit` do not modify this path.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `strcmp` compares `oid` against the 21-character `PBKDF2_OID` string plus its NUL terminator; only 19 bytes of `oid` were initialized from the decoded inner OID text.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in `__interceptor_memcmp` at offset 19 inside a 22-byte region and attributes the poisoned data to the stack allocation of `oid` in `read_pbkdf2_params`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant bytes are created when external libtasn1 copies only the short textual OID into caller buffer `oid`, leaving the rest of the preallocated 128-byte stack buffer untouched.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is accepted as DER `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo`; on the witnessed path the caller requested decryption, so the code continues into the encrypted-key parser.

coarse_trace.summary: Aliases the attacker-controlled DER bytes into `_data` and routes the encrypted witness into `pkcs8_key_decode`.
Reads the outer PKCS#8 encryption-algorithm OID, classifies it as `PBES2_GENERIC`, and finds the DER subspan for `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters`.
Uses the saved schema state to enter the PBES2 branch and decodes the PBES2 parameter block into ASN.1 object `pasn`.
Allocates `oid` without initialization, external libtasn1 copies only the short inner-OID string into it, and `strcmp` reads the untouched tail.

fine_trace.note: Copies the attacker-controlled DER pointer and byte count into local datum `_data`, creating the exact byte span later decoded on the crashing path.
Decodes that byte span as `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo`. On the witnessed path the caller requested decryption, so the admitted ASN.1 object proceeds into `pkcs8_key_decrypt`.
Reads the outer PKCS#8 `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` OID into `enc_oid`. In the witness blob this field is the PBES2 OID `1.2.840.113549.1.5.13`.
Compares `enc_oid` with `PBES2_OID` and returns `PBES2_GENERIC` on the witnessed path.
Stores the classifier result in local `schema`, so later parameter parsing branches on this saved state rather than on `enc_oid` directly.

fine_trace.code: result = asn1_der_decoding_startEnd(pkcs8_asn, raw_key->data, raw_key->size, "encryptionAlgorithm.parameters", &params_start, &params_end); params_len = params_end - params_start + 1;
fine_trace.note: Locates the DER subspan for `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` inside the attacker-controlled PKCS#8 blob and computes `params_len`, producing the exact bytes later parsed as PBES2 parameters.
Gates PBES2 parsing on the saved schema state. Because step 5 stored `PBES2_GENERIC`, the function enters the PBES2-specific branch on the witnessed path.
Decodes the `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` subspan as `PKIX1.pkcs-5-PBES2-params`, materializing ASN.1 object `pasn` that contains the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` field.

fine_trace.code: result = asn1_get_object_id_der(der + counter, ider_len, &len2, temp, sizeof(temp)); tlen = strlen(temp); if (tlen > 0) _asn1_set_value(p, temp, tlen + 1);
fine_trace.note: During step 8's decode, external libtasn1 converts the inner OID bytes `20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff` into the textual value `0.32.32.32.2097056` and stores that short string in the ASN.1 node. The final `ff ff ff` continuation run never terminates with a byte lacking bit 0x80, so it contributes no appended arc.
Allocates the 128-byte stack buffer that will receive the textual KDF OID, but leaves every byte indeterminate until later writes initialize them.
Requests the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` string from `pasn` and offers the whole `oid` buffer as the destination.

External libtasn1's `PUT_STR_VALUE` macro sets `*len = strlen(node->value) + 1` and copies exactly that many bytes via `_asn1_strcpy`. On this call `node->value` is the 18-character string from step 9 and `value == oid`, so only 19 bytes including the NUL are initialized and bytes 19..127 of `oid` stay indeterminate.

Compares `oid` with the 22-byte `PBKDF2_OID` literal (21 characters plus NUL). Because step 12 initialized only 19 bytes including NUL, `strcmp` reads three poisoned tail bytes; MSAN reports the first uninitialized byte at offset 19 inside that 22-byte region and attributes it to `oid`'s stack allocation.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer reports the uninitialized value as created by allocation of `oid` in the stack frame at line 647; the actual `oid` declaration in the vulnerable source is line 651.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` reproduces the MemorySanitizer crash recorded in `sanitizer_trace.txt`: importing the raw DER blob through `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8(key, &raw, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, "password", 0)` reaches `read_pbkdf2_params` and triggers the uninitialized read in `strcmp(oid, PBKDF2_OID)`.

format.name: DER EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo (PKCS#8)
format.contract: A 444-byte DER `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` whose outer `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` field is the PBES2 OID `06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 05 0d`, and whose nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` field is the exact malformed OBJECT IDENTIFIER `06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff`. In the staged build, external `../libtasn1/lib/decoding.c` stores that inner OID as `0.32.32.32.2097056`, and external `../libtasn1/lib/element.c` therefore copies only 19 bytes including the NUL into `char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE]` before `strcmp(oid, PBKDF2_OID)` consumes a 22-byte compare window.
